mathematical_reason: ProofWiki defines the Borel sigma-algebra of a topological space as sigma(τ), the sigma-algebra generated by its open sets. This is not an arbitrary sigma-algebra. The metric-space variant is the same construction with the metric-induced topology; no chosen metric is required here.

ProofWiki states that adjacency matrix entries encode edge counts, with simple-graph entries 0 or 1, symmetric undirected matrices, and zero diagonal when loops are excluded. An ordering of vertices determines indices. Directed, weighted, multigraph and loop conventions are different contexts.

A bipartition need not have all possible edges between its parts, so this is not a complete bipartite graph. The existence condition may allow an empty part. The property and a graph equipped with a particular partition are contextually related but not identical data.

ProofWiki's primary Boolean ring definition is an idempotent ring with unity. It does not require additional commutativity as an axiom because the ring axioms plus universal idempotence imply commutativity. Distinguish from the alternative definition without a unity requirement.

ProofWiki explicitly records an alternative Boolean ring definition that does not impose the existence of unity. A unital Boolean ring is a special case, but a nonunital idempotent ring need not have any identity. Both mathematically correct conventions must remain separately visible.
